original_question: Let X_n^d be the space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n with nonzero discriminant, and let Phi assign to each such form its associated form of degree n(d-2) on the dual space. For every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d, does there exist a rational GL_n-invariant function R on the space of degree n(d-2) associated forms, defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d), such that R composed with Phi equals S?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: the strong associated-form invariants conjecture for homogeneous forms with nonvanishing discriminant.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies the discriminant-open locus X_n^d, the associated-form morphism Phi, the target degree n(d-2), the GL_n-invariance on both sides, and—crucially—the stronger requirement that the target rational invariant be defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d), not merely on a dense open set. Those are the features that distinguish the paper's open conjecture from the weaker variant proved nearby.
missing_details: State the ambient source space explicitly as Q_n^d = Sym^d((C^n)^*) (equivalently, the space of homogeneous degree-d polynomials on C^n).
State the standing assumptions n >= 2 and d >= 3.
Define X_n^d precisely as X_n^d = {f in Q_n^d : Delta(f) != 0}, where Delta is the discriminant.
Specify the target precisely as Q_n^{n(d-2)*}, i.e. the space of degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space (C^n)^*; if one identifies (C^n)^{**} with C^n, say so explicitly.
Make clear that Phi is the associated-form morphism attached to f (via its Milnor algebra / Macaulay inverse system), not an arbitrary assignment.
Specify that S belongs to the algebra of regular GL_n(C)-invariant functions C[X_n^d]^{GL_n(C)}.
Specify that R is a GL_n(C)-invariant rational function on Q_n^{n(d-2)*} that is required to be defined at every point of the image Phi(X_n^d), even if it is not regular on all of Q_n^{n(d-2)*}.
State explicitly that the identity R o Phi = S is required on all of X_n^d.
Indicate that this is the stronger/open conjectural form, whereas the nearby theorem proves only the weaker variant without the full everywhere-defined-on-Phi(X_n^d) extension requirement.
There is no nilpotency condition, no 'sufficiently large m' qualifier, and no characteristic-p variant in this statement; the field is C throughout.
refined_question: For integers n >= 2 and d >= 3, let Q_n^d := Sym^d((C^n)^*) be the vector space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, let X_n^d := {f in Q_n^d : Delta(f) != 0} be the discriminant-nonvanishing locus, and let Phi: X_n^d -> Q_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism, where Q_n^{n(d-2)*} denotes the space of degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space (C^n)^*. Is it true that for every regular GL_n(C)-invariant function S in C[X_n^d]^{GL_n(C)}, there exists a GL_n(C)-invariant rational function R on Q_n^{n(d-2)*}, defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d), such that R(Phi(f)) = S(f) for all f in X_n^d?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's Conjecture 1.1, not at the weaker nearby theorem. What fixes this identification is the explicit demand that the target-side invariant be defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d); the paper treats that as the stronger conjectural extension beyond the weaker variant proved in full generality. The needed sharpening is mostly notational and scopal: the paper works over C, with Q_n^d = Sym^d((C^n)^*), X_n^d cut out by the nonvanishing of the discriminant, and Phi landing in degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))
